description: Builds asymmetric induction from competing chiral transition states, quantifies enantiomeric excess, and explains enamine/iminium and metal-catalyzed approaches with analytic limits.

related_resources.reason: Defines enantioselective and diastereoselective product formation.
Chiral centers, enantiomers and structural requirements for molecular chirality.
2021 recognition of List and MacMillan and development of asymmetric organocatalysis.

historical_claims.anchor: The major-to-minor ratio is nine to one, and the enantiomeric excess is eighty percent
A suitable secondary amine can reversibly react with a ketone or aldehyde to generate an enamine-like nucleophile.
The 2021 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognized Benjamin List and David MacMillan

authorship.scope: Original organic synthesis and selectivity lecture, scientific companion and source-linked catalog metadata.

background: Introductory organic molecular structure, carbonyls, bonding and reaction mechanisms. All additional specialist ideas are introduced in the narration.
readiness_checks: Why is 90% major enantiomer only 80% ee?
Why is a chiral catalyst needed when two enantiomeric faces are otherwise equally accessible?
